tagline: grill me with ancient greek – curated tools for learners of Ancient Greek

tools.name: Logeion
tools.desc: A one-stop lookup portal: the LSJ, Middle Liddell, Pape, Slater lexica plus automatic morphology analysis for the word you look up.
tools.use_when: You need a word's full lexicographic entry (LSJ), or want several lexica side by side.

tools.name: Wiktionary – Ancient Greek
tools.desc: Quick glosses and declension tables edited by the community; good for getting the basic sense of a word.
tools.use_when: You want a fast first answer; cross-check against LSJ via Logeion, since entries are community-written.

tools.name: Diogenes
tools.desc: Open-source desktop application that reads the LSJ and Slater lexica offline; works without a network connection (you supply the dictionary data files yourself).
tools.use_when: You want offline LSJ lookup at native speed, with Greek-text support.

tools.name: Perseus Digital Library (Tufts)
tools.desc: The oldest open digital library of Ancient Greek texts with English translations; includes a word study tool that parses each word.
tools.use_when: You want to read a text with translation and cite a passage by author and work.

tools.name: Scaife Viewer
tools.desc: The modern interface to the Perseus 5.0 corpus: click a word to see its morphology, read a facing translation, and build vocabulary lists per passage.
tools.use_when: You want the smoothest reading experience with in-text morphology (recommended for beginners).

tools.name: Theoi Classical Texts Library
tools.desc: A library of Greek originals with English translations, organized by mythological figure and by author; public-domain sources.
tools.use_when: You are reading mythological texts or hunting a passage by character/author.

tools.name: Greek Wikisource
tools.desc: Community-proofed transcriptions of Greek texts (ancient and modern), interface in Modern Greek.
tools.use_when: You need a transcription when Perseus/Scaife do not have the work.

tools.name: TypeGreek
tools.desc: Type polytonic Greek on a Latin keyboard: type the letters, then press the accent/breathing keys to combine.
tools.use_when: You need to type a few words or sentences on a machine without a Greek keyboard.

tools.name: Keyman – Greek keyboards
tools.desc: Greek keyboard layouts (including fully polytonic ones) for Windows, macOS, Linux and mobile.
tools.use_when: You type Greek regularly, in any application. Tip: Windows and macOS both ship a built-in "Greek Polytonic" keyboard in the system language settings.

tools.name: Gentium Plus (SIL)
tools.desc: A free font with full polytonic Greek support (accents, breathings, iota subscript) that displays beautifully in lessons and texts.
tools.use_when: Greek renders poorly or without diacritics on your machine → install this font and set it as the default for Greek text.

tools.name: Graecum VN lessons
tools.desc: A complete 48-lesson course: every lesson has confusable-pairs tables, self-study exercises, and answer keys that appear only when printing (Ctrl+P → Save as PDF). Vietnamese main edition; English edition under way.
tools.use_when: You are following the roadmap; this toolkit is the gear you use alongside those lessons.

tools.name: Anki
tools.desc: The reference-standard spaced-repetition program for vocabulary. Official Graecum VN decks will be released in the graecum-vn repository (roadmap part 6).
tools.use_when: You are drilling the ★ vocabulary of each lesson on a scientifically spaced schedule.

tools.name: Smyth – A Greek Grammar for Colleges (1920)
tools.desc: The standard reference grammar of Ancient Greek (Herbert Weir Smyth, public domain), in an easy-to-navigate electronic edition; ~1500 numbered sections.
tools.use_when: You need to research a grammar point beyond the scope of the lessons – use the index of subjects.

tools.name: Smyth on the Perseus Hopper
tools.desc: Smyth on Perseus: read by section number, cross-linked with the Perseus text library.
tools.use_when: You are reading on Perseus and want to consult the grammar without leaving the page.

tools.name: Smyth 1920 – scanned copy
tools.desc: The original scan on the Internet Archive – a fallback whenever the electronic editions change address.
tools.use_when: You need the original PD text for scholarly citation.

tools.name: Project resource comparison tables
tools.desc: Comparisons of reference grammars, introductory textbooks and lexica – with recommendations per level; link-only policy for copyrighted works.
tools.use_when: You want to choose supplementary material beyond the lessons.

tools.name: Terminology (English glossary)
tools.desc: Glossary of the standard English grammatical terms for Ancient Greek (writing system, nouns, verbs, syntax, Greek-vs-Latin contrasts), each entry cross-referenced with the Vietnamese terminology used in the Graecum VN lessons.
tools.use_when: You need the correct English search key for LSJ/Smyth, or the Vietnamese-English mapping of a grammatical term.
